functions.name: bit_scan_forward32
functions.signature: int bit_scan_forward32(unsigned int v);
functions.description: Returns the index (0-based) of the least significant set bit in v. This is a macro alias that maps at compile time to an architecture-selected implementation (ASM, de Bruijn, or branch-based). Value is undefined if v == 0.
requirements: v must be non-zero; the return value is undefined for v == 0 (per header documentation).
This identifier is a macro; which implementation it calls depends on build-time macros (e.g., CC_GCC_LIKE_ASM, __CPU_x86, __CPU_x86_64, BIT_SCAN_DEBRUIJN, BIT_SCAN_BRANCH).
If the de Bruijn implementation is selected, the program must link definitions for _debruijn_hash32 in bit_scan.c.

functions.name: bit_scan_forward64
functions.signature: int bit_scan_forward64(unsigned long long v);
functions.description: Returns the index (0-based) of the least significant set bit in v (64-bit). Macro alias to an architecture-selected implementation. Value is undefined if v == 0.
requirements: v must be non-zero; the return value is undefined for v == 0.
This identifier is a macro; selected implementation depends on build-time macros.
If the de Bruijn implementation is selected, the program must link definitions for _debruijn_hash64 in bit_scan.c.

functions.name: bit_scan_reverse32
functions.signature: int bit_scan_reverse32(unsigned int v);
functions.description: Returns the index (0-based) of the most significant set bit in v. Macro alias to an architecture-selected implementation. Value is undefined if v == 0.
requirements: v must be non-zero; the return value is undefined for v == 0.
This identifier is a macro; selected implementation depends on build-time macros.
If the de Bruijn implementation is selected (reverse_debruijn variant), the program must link definitions for _debruijn_hash32 in bit_scan.c.

functions.name: bit_scan_reverse64
functions.signature: int bit_scan_reverse64(unsigned long long v);
functions.description: Returns the index (0-based) of the most significant set bit in v (64-bit). Macro alias to an architecture-selected implementation. Value is undefined if v == 0.
requirements: v must be non-zero; the return value is undefined for v == 0.
This identifier is a macro; selected implementation depends on build-time macros.
If the de Bruijn implementation is selected (reverse_debruijn variant), the program must link definitions for _debruijn_hash64 in bit_scan.c.

functions.name: bit_scan_forward
functions.signature: int bit_scan_forward(unsigned long v);
functions.description: Returns the index (0-based) of the least significant set bit in v. Macro that maps to bit_scan_forward32 or bit_scan_forward64 depending on the size of unsigned long (via ULONG_MAX or LP64). Value is undefined if v == 0.
requirements: v must be non-zero; the return value is undefined for v == 0.
This is a macro that dispatches to 32-bit or 64-bit variants based on platform; the underlying implementation then follows the respective requirements (e.g., potential need for de Bruijn tables).

functions.name: bit_scan_reverse
functions.signature: int bit_scan_reverse(unsigned long v);
functions.description: Returns the index (0-based) of the most significant set bit in v. Macro that maps to bit_scan_reverse32 or bit_scan_reverse64 depending on the size of unsigned long (via ULONG_MAX or LP64). Value is undefined if v == 0.
requirements: v must be non-zero; the return value is undefined for v == 0.
This is a macro that dispatches to 32-bit or 64-bit variants based on platform; the underlying implementation then follows the respective requirements (e.g., potential need for de Bruijn tables).

functions.name: bit_scan_reverse_debruijn32
functions.signature: static inline int bit_scan_reverse_debruijn32(unsigned int v);
functions.description: Returns the index (0-based) of the most significant set bit in v using a de Bruijn sequence method. Iteratively clears the lowest set bit to isolate the highest and looks up its index via a precomputed table.
requirements: v must be non-zero; behavior/return is undefined for v == 0 (per general contract in header).
Requires that the extern table _debruijn_hash32[32] is defined and initialized at link time (provided by bit_scan.c).

functions.name: bit_scan_reverse_debruijn64
functions.signature: static inline int bit_scan_reverse_debruijn64(unsigned long long v);
functions.description: Returns the index (0-based) of the most significant set bit in v using a 64-bit de Bruijn sequence method. Iteratively clears bits to isolate the highest set bit and uses a precomputed lookup table.
requirements: v must be non-zero; behavior/return is undefined for v == 0.
Requires that the extern table _debruijn_hash64[64] is defined and initialized at link time (provided by bit_scan.c).

functions.name: bit_scan_forward_slow32
functions.signature: static inline int bit_scan_forward_slow32(unsigned int v);
functions.description: Reference implementation that scans from LSB to MSB to find the first set bit (0-based index). Intended for testing/verification; slower than other methods.
requirements: v should be non-zero to obtain a meaningful index; if v == 0, the function returns 0 but that value is not a valid index for v == 0 (per overall header note of undefined for zero).

functions.name: bit_scan_reverse_slow32
functions.signature: static inline int bit_scan_reverse_slow32(unsigned int v);
functions.description: Reference implementation that scans from MSB to LSB to find the last set bit (0-based index). Intended for testing/verification; slower than other methods.
requirements: v should be non-zero to obtain a meaningful index; if v == 0, the function returns 0 but that value is not meaningful (per header’s undefined for zero).

functions.description: Reference implementation that scans from LSB to MSB to find the first set bit (0-based index) for 64-bit values. Intended for testing/verification; slower than other methods.
requirements: v should be non-zero to obtain a meaningful index; if v == 0, the function returns 0 but that value is not meaningful (per header’s undefined for zero).

functions.signature: static inline int bit_scan_reverse_slow64(unsigned long long v);
functions.description: Reference implementation that scans from MSB to LSB to find the last set bit (0-based index) for 64-bit values. Intended for testing/verification; slower than other methods.
requirements: v should be non-zero to obtain a meaningful index; if v == 0, the function returns 0 but that value is not meaningful (per header’s undefined for zero).

functions.name: bit_scan_forward_br32
functions.signature: static inline int bit_scan_forward_br32(unsigned int v);
functions.description: Branch-based method to return the index (0-based) of the least significant set bit in v using a sequence of masks and shifts. Faster than slow/reference in many cases.
requirements: v should be non-zero; the returned value is undefined for v == 0 (the implementation produces a value that is not meaningful).

functions.name: bit_scan_forward_asm32
functions.signature: static inline int bit_scan_forward_asm32(unsigned int v);
functions.description: x86 inline-assembly implementation using BSF to return the index (0-based) of the least significant set bit in a 32-bit value. Available only when BIT_SCAN_ASM is enabled (GCC-like inline asm on x86/x86_64).
requirements: v must be non-zero; BSF result is undefined for zero input.
Available only if BIT_SCAN_ASM is defined (requires CC_GCC_LIKE_ASM and __CPU_x86 or __CPU_x86_64).

functions.name: bit_scan_reverse_asm32
functions.signature: static inline int bit_scan_reverse_asm32(unsigned int v);
functions.description: x86 inline-assembly implementation using BSR to return the index (0-based) of the most significant set bit in a 32-bit value. Available only when BIT_SCAN_ASM is enabled (GCC-like inline asm on x86/x86_64).
requirements: v must be non-zero; BSR result is undefined for zero input.
Available only if BIT_SCAN_ASM is defined (requires CC_GCC_LIKE_ASM and __CPU_x86 or __CPU_x86_64).

functions.name: bit_scan_forward_asm64
functions.signature: static inline int bit_scan_forward_asm64(unsigned long long v);
functions.description: 64-bit implementation of BSF to return the index (0-based) of the least significant set bit in a 64-bit value. On __CPU_x86_64 it uses bsfq; otherwise it falls back to two 32-bit scans. Available only when BIT_SCAN_ASM is enabled.
requirements: v must be non-zero; BSF result is undefined for zero input.
Available only if BIT_SCAN_ASM is defined (requires CC_GCC_LIKE_ASM and __CPU_x86 or __CPU_x86_64).

functions.name: bit_scan_reverse_asm64
functions.signature: static inline int bit_scan_reverse_asm64(unsigned long long v);
functions.description: 64-bit implementation of BSR to return the index (0-based) of the most significant set bit in a 64-bit value. On __CPU_x86_64 it uses bsrq; otherwise it falls back to two 32-bit scans. Available only when BIT_SCAN_ASM is enabled.
requirements: v must be non-zero; BSR result is undefined for zero input.
Available only if BIT_SCAN_ASM is defined (requires CC_GCC_LIKE_ASM and __CPU_x86 or __CPU_x86_64).

functions.name: bit_count
functions.signature: static inline int bit_count(unsigned int u);
functions.description: Returns the number of 1 bits (Hamming weight) in u. Implemented either via the POPCNT instruction (when enabled and available on x86/x86_64 with SSE4.2 and GCC-like inline asm) or via a portable SW bit-parallel method.
requirements: No special constraints on u; valid for all 32-bit unsigned inputs; return range is 0..32.
The ASM version is available only if BIT_COUNT_ASM is defined (requires CC_GCC_LIKE_ASM, x86/x86_64, and __SSE4_2__). Otherwise the portable inline implementation is used.
